title: Finite diagonalizable group scheme by its natural character functor
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $G$ a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Say that $G$ is finite diagonalizable if there is a finite abelian group $M$ and, for every $k$-scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], a group isomorphism $e_T:G(T)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{grp}}(M,\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times)$, natural in $T$: for every $k$-morphism $t:T\to U$ and $x\in G(U)$, $e_T(x\circ t)=(\Gamma(t)^\times)\circ e_U(x)$. The group law on $M$ may be written multiplicatively. Equivalently $G$ is isomorphic as a $k$-group scheme to $D_k(M)=\operatorname{Spec}k[M]$, with group-algebra comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $e_m\mapsto1$ and antipode $e_m\mapsto e_{m^{-1}}$. Over an algebraically closed field this is precisely a finite group scheme of multiplicative type.
